The economic evidence submitted in this proceeding underscores what is apparent to the most casual observer travelling a "loop" or "beltway" around the circumference of a modern city - municipal political bounds have not kept pace with the movement of people to suburban residential developments and of business and industry to the suburban shopping center and industrial park. Consequently, we conclude that existing rules and regulations no longer reflect the zone which is "adjacent to and commercially a part of" base municipalities.
It is argued that in view of the Commission's policy to extend automatically zone limits as central cities annex more land, there is little reason to grant an across-the-board expansion of commercial zone limits. Annexation is not a viable alternative for many cities since they are hemmed in by incorporated suburban communities.
